Manufactured and Intellectual Capital
KCB Group’s manufactured capital consists of cutting-edge digital systems, tools (proced
and rules), and our operational philosophy, all of which help to speed the flow of knowledge
information both within the Group and to external parties such as suppliers and distribu
channels.
These capitals are in form of leased or totally owned systems and whose value is earned thro
the delivery of products and services. Our strong distribution network, which includes the regi
largest branch network as well as cutting-edge digital platforms, is a key source of compet
difference. KCB Group was able to continue providing service to our clients despite the challen
posed by the COVID-19 pandemic by leveraging on its digital platforms, which include mo
internet, agents, and merchants.
Our clients are aware of and appreciate our organizational efficiency. Hence, efficient operati
processes are just as important as innovative products and contact channels.
We remained a top-tier financial institution in the area because of our continued investment in
digital space, providing new solutions, improving ease of access to banking services, and ensu
system availability and reliability. To manage results generated by manufactured capitals we k
optimising our structures, systems, processes, and tools.
Intellectual capital on the other hand, is a collection of factors such as how the brand is regar

intellectual property, technical know-how, and the ability to be creative and innovative in
delivery of products and technology deployment. As a forward-thinking Bank, we place a
value on intellectual capital to gain a competitive advantage. For the firm to remain adapt
and sustainable, products and services must be reflective of ever-evolving industry pract
(technology or otherwise). Furthermore, through rigorous stakeholder engagement, regula
compliance, and a strategic communications approach, the Group guarantees that its reputa
credentials stay strong.
In this regard, the Bank has continued to outperform the market on key
intellectual capital metrics. Every year, the Bank’s research arm conducts
a brand health assessment, identifying top brand drivers and stress spots,
as well as specific remedial steps.
